summary: Reader labels D1 and D3 are normalized to inherited sense numbers 1 and 3, with detransitive=true on added examples. Existing main-list sense 3 remains unchanged; no old sense is renumbered.

Detransitive contrasts agentless destruction with active indefinite plural agents. JTM 3.2/20 contrasts conditional qšiʕi and məqšoʕi; 67/135 has extinction without a stated agent; 27/35 is active unspecified plural, not Detransitive.
Preterit-wa qšəʕwayle is attested independently at 56/19 and 113/77. Talay 2/28 gqəšʕowa is counterfactual Infectum-wa, with collective feminine agreement and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe.
Cognate qšoʕo combines with active Infectum (95/86), active Preterit (95/220), and Detransitive Preterit (113/70). Edition translations compress the emphasis; they are preserved unchanged.

Plural patient indexing in qšiʕile at 95/220 is supported by the overt L-marked agent and corroborates the provisional active reading at 112/29. Do not classify a form as Detransitive solely because of i.

No new idiom is required: clothing/bread/soil removal is compositional, reciprocal destruction is already represented, and the uncertain eye metaphor remains a research extension rather than a published idiom.
Jan English is project machine translation, not an edition translation. Senses rest on Turoyo alone; quoted English retains the supplied wording. This JSON contains only round-2 proposals.
Round-1 childlessness sense 4 and economic-ruin 3b remain intact; the new active expulsion sense is numbered 5.
The own-eyes image at Jan 1.42/1857 is in a Turoyo rendering of an Arabic quotation. It documents this text and possible contact, not an independent origin in Turoyo.
Qšəʕiwo l bə Yawse at Jan 1.10/404 has unresolved vowel/voice and family coding. No Detransitive Preterit-wa box is published from it.
Jan 1.21/1012 expresses destruction for honour/religion, without economic loss; it does not independently support round-1 economic ruin 3b.
Round-1 extinction and extermination cells already have five or more examples. Jan is selected only for remaining gaps or distinct constructions.

29/232 includes embedded “223,” and the eye complaint cited in the entry as 29/233, but the supplied German stops before it. Verify segmentation and the missing translation before a figurative reassignment; no new quotation made.
MAC NE Mar Dumet/22: what is final -yo in qušʕátteyo? Retain its exact spelling and dependent intention frame.
MAC Ishaq Material culture/45: confirm the roller/clay subject-object relation and negative-purpose scope; withhold this less transparent example.
112/29 qšiʕile: confirm active plural patient indexing versus Detransitive plus dative; 95/220 favors the active analysis.
Inherited (İlyas p.c.) and PrS page/line references are retained. The supplied modern PrS text/verse references are not silently substituted for them.
Does Jan 1.42/1854 explicitly distinguish expulsion from extermination, or use an extermination threat rhetorically? The new sense rests on the overt place-removal context.
Parse Qšəʕiwo l bə Yawse at Jan 1.10/404: active indefinite plural or Detransitive, and displacement or extinction?

summary: Bread, garments, grass, skin and the soil surface extend physical removal beyond eyes. An instrument can be the subject (plough blade). No baking or ploughing technical sense is required.

29/232 embeds an eye-removal complaint already quoted as 29/233. Humiliation/loss of standing is plausible, but absent German and inconsistent segmentation prevent a secure figurative reclassification.
